name: Rhabdoid Tumor Predisposition Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Rhabdoid Tumor Predisposition Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of a pathogenic germline mutation in SMARCB1 or SMARCA4 genes
Diagnosis of rhabdoid tumor (e.g., atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor or malignant rhabdoid tumor) before age 5
Family history of rhabdoid tumors or related malignancies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a pathogenic germline SMARCB1 or SMARCA4 mutation plus diagnosis of rhabdoid tumor before age 5
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for confirmation; clinical suspicion should prompt molecular analysis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor (AT/RT) of the central nervous system
Malignant rhabdoid tumor of the kidney
Malignant rhabdoid tumor of soft tissues

common.symptomName: Neurological deficits related to CNS tumor location
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to tumor location

common.symptomName: Abdominal distension or palpable renal mass
Constitutional symptoms including weight loss and failure to thrive

occasional.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to CNS tumor obstruction
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain from tumor

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to thoracic soft tissue tumors
searchTerms: respiratory distress due to chest masses
trouble breathing from thoracic soft tissue growths

occasional.symptomName: Anemia related to bone marrow involvement or chronic disease
searchTerms: low red blood cell count from bone marrow disease

rare.symptomName: Ophthalmological abnormalities such as proptosis from orbital tumors
searchTerms: protruding eyes due to eye socket mass

laboratory: Loss of INI1 (SMARCB1) protein expression on immunohistochemistry
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in some cases
imaging: MRI or CT showing aggressive CNS masses with heterogeneous enhancement
Renal ultrasound or CT revealing renal masses
Soft tissue masses on MRI or CT with rapid growth
other: Histopathology demonstrating rhabdoid tumor morphology with characteristic cytoplasmic inclusions

redFlags: Diagnosis of rhabdoid tumor before age 5
Family history of rhabdoid tumors or early childhood malignancies
Presence of multiple primary rhabdoid tumors or synchronous tumors
references: Biegel JA et al. Rhabdoid Tumor Predisposition Syndrome. GeneReviews. 2020.
Orphanet: Rhabdoid Tumor Predisposition Syndrome. ORPHA:231108.
Versteege I et al. SMARCB1 mutations in rhabdoid tumors. Nat Genet. 1998.
